question: We are building a portfolio of UK nature-based carbon projects that we may later tokenise. For East Anglia, compare the expected abatement per hectare and its uncertainty for a Peatland Code rewetting project on Fenland cropland, a new Corsican pine woodland near Thetford of the kind registered under the Woodland Carbon Code, and hedgerow agroforestry on Fenland farms. How well validated is each model, and which project type is the most robust basis for credits?

assumptions.assumption: Baseline is drained Fenland cropland under the DT8 Fenland water-table climatology (~0.66 m), crops winter wheat (WW) and potato as bracketing arable cases at typical fertiliser rates.
assumptions.rationale: Peatland Code baseline is the current drained land use; WW and potato are common Fen crops.

assumptions.assumption: Rewetting to reed (paludiculture/wet fen) with annual mean water table 0.05-0.10 m below surface; established regime (3 years since rewetting) plus a first-year check; AR6 GWP100 as DT8 uses.
assumptions.rationale: Typical Peatland Code rewetted-fen target water table; DT8 reed class.

assumptions.assumption: New Corsican pine (CP) planted 2026 on bare land at Thetford, 100 ha, 50-year horizon, no-intervention and thin-and-fell regimes, both growth models, landscape-calibrated productivity.
assumptions.rationale: Represents a typical WCC project near Thetford; 50 years is within common WCC crediting periods.

assumptions.assumption: DT6 'fens' pilot tile stands in for Fenland farms; 1,000 new trees planted in 2025 (run as both 'hedgerow' and 'agroforestry' kinds), 50 years. Per-hectare values derived assuming 100 trees per ha of farmland (i.e. ~10 ha), stated as a derived illustration.
assumptions.rationale: DT6 models per tree, not per hectare; density is a project design choice, so results are scaled transparently.

assumptions.assumption: Abatement for peat is avoided emissions (baseline minus project, t CO2e/ha/yr); for trees it is removals (net CO2 flux, negative = removal). Annualised over the horizon for comparison. Model estimates only, not credits.
assumptions.rationale: Different credit mechanics (emission reduction vs removal).

assumptions: Calibrated on ESA Biomass CCI v7 only (no GEDI, ICESat-2, lidar or other satellite data).

Woodland mask from the NFI woodland map GB 2024; species groups, planting years (stand ages) and Forestry England yield classes from the FE sub-compartment database. FE yield class is only an independent check, never used in calibration.
Pixels outside the FE estate take a species group from the NFI forest type (conifer, felled and young types: the landscape's dominant conifer; broadleaved types: mixed broadleaves).
3-PG climate: HadUK-Grid 1991-2020 monthly averages (Met Office portal, ~2 km and 12 km grids); radiation estimated from the diurnal temperature range (Hargreaves-Samani).
CCI v7 saturates at about 150 Mg/ha in these forests; calibration compares CCI with min(model AGB, 150). Each pixel is treated as an unthinned even-aged stand.

provenance.parameters: calibrated baseline: crown-by-crown EA lidar calibration in fens
assumptions: Inventory: National Trees Outside Woodland map V1 (lone trees, groups of trees, small woodlands; canopy > 3 m outside NFI woodland). NFI overhanging canopy is left to DT4, hedges below 3 m to DT5.
Calibrated on Environment Agency lidar canopy heights only: first and last return of the National LIDAR Programme and last-return LIDAR Tiles DSMs back to 1998, all above the NLP terrain model.
Biomass from crown size and height with Jucker et al. (2017); trees in groups share the object's crown area equally; leaf type is a pilot prior (no open leaf-type map for TOW).
Crown light-use model climate: HadUK-Grid 1991-2020 monthly averages; radiation from Hargreaves-Samani.
Trees removed before the TOW map was made (2016-2023 lidar) are not in the inventory, so their loss is not seen.

Shipped results from scripts/calibrate_pilots.py.

Woodland: new Corsican pine at Thetford, 50-year mean net CO2 removal, low/high = annualised 90 % ensemble range [R5, R6]. Hedgerow/agroforestry: Fens pilot, 1,000 trees scaled to 100 trees/ha (derived), 90 % range [R8, R9]. Model estimates, not credits.
